title: Existing-Home Sales (NAR, November 2026 data) — the residential half of the 2026-12-09 GDPNow vintage, 10:00 a.m. ET on FOMC decision day
source: IR: the publisher's own forward calendar — nar.realtor/newsroom/nar-statistical-news-release-schedule, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 483,177 bytes), whose 2026 table reads verbatim "DECEMBER | Wed., Dec. 9 | November Existing-Home Sales" under the page's standing note "All releases at 10 a.m. Eastern Time", and its downloadable twin /sites/default/files/2025-11/2026-nar-statistical-news-release-schedule.docx (HTTP 200, 55,384 bytes, published 2025-11), which carries the full year and the same December row. Promoted from the `EST:` single-source proposal filed 2026-09-06 by the wholesale-trade-2026-12-09 sweep: that lane could not find NAR's schedule (it tried /newsroom/release-schedule, 404) and rested the date on the Atlanta Fed's incorporation calendar alone; the real path is linked from the existing-home-sales statistics page as "NAR Research Data Release Dates". Corroborated three ways: the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates 2026-12-09 10:00 row reads "Wholesale trade, Existing-home sales"; the seven 2026 EHS release dates the GDPNow ContribArchives free text names (01-14, 02-12, 03-10, 04-13, 05-11, 06-09, 07-09) match NAR's published 2026 schedule 7 for 7; and NAR's live statistics page independently states the next edition ("August 2026 will be released on Thursday, September 10, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern"), the same schedule's September row. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The calendar's first housing print, and the residential half of a shared GDPNow vintage whose other half (wholesale-trade-2026-12-09) owns a different line. Measured 2026-09-06 from GDPTrackingModelDataAndForecasts.xlsx ContribArchives (1,871 vintages 2014-05-01 -> 2026-07-28 = 1,822 same-quarter deltas): the 140 vintages naming an existing-home-sales release move the residential-investment contribution a median 0.0376pp against 0.0057pp for the other 1,682 (permutation p<0.0001) while moving change-in-inventory-investment 0.0001pp against 0.0197pp, and on 92.9% of them the residential move is the larger of the two against a 36.5% base rate. That is the model's own wiring, not an inference: the workbook's Residential sheet routes `valExHomeSales` ("Real value of existing home sales") into `FRSBKX_USNAqtr` ("Brokerage commissions"), because an existing home is a transfer of an existing asset and only the commission is output. So the 12-09 vintage is separable, not muddled — inventories belong to the wholesale print and residential to this one. `symbols: []` is a MEASURED finding rather than an assumption: across 122 EHS release days since 2016 the homebuilder ETFs are inert (ITB median session range 1.911% vs a 1.839% baseline, p=0.40; XHB 1.693% vs 1.629%, p=0.46; SPY 0.894% vs 0.874%, p=0.75), while the same names move hard on the FOMC decision this print shares its day with (ITB 2.918% on the 22 SEP decision days, p=0.0003). Impact stays `low`: no house playbook is macro- or housing-keyed and no instrument attaches. Date is `confirmed` on the publisher's own calendar; that licenses nothing on its own, and the ledger's call is stand aside. Discovered in the wholesale-trade-2026-12-09 adjacency sweep 2026-09-06; canonical file written by this event's own initial research the same day, which shadows that proposal.
